fixes.explanation: Worships. After David got up from the ground, washed and anointed himself, and changed his clothes, he “…went into the house of the LORD and worshiped.” That comes before he asks for any food. The child had just died, and the first place he goes is to the LORD.

True. After worshiping, David “…went to his own house, and at his request they set food before him, and he ate.” David asks, and they bring it. He had been fasting while the child was alive, so this is a change.

Rich and poor, that's how Nathan sets it up. He's the prophet the LORD sent to David, and he opens with two men in one city and a gap between them you can see from space. No fancy words needed. The text says it right there: “…one rich and the other poor.”
Nathan never says a word about age. The only difference he gives is “…one rich and the other poor.” The story sticks to money. Keep your eyes on the bank accounts, not the birthdays.

A servant works for you, and this lamb never punched a clock. The text says it was “…like a daughter to him.” A lamb that drinks from your cup is not on the payroll, friend. The text says it shared his food and slept in his arms.
Brother is a fair guess, since it sounds close. But the text says the lamb was “…like a daughter to him.” Daughter is the word it uses. I think the poor man's heart was all in on that little lamb.

“You are that man!” Nathan tells David. David had just said the man in the story deserves to die, and Nathan turns that verdict around on him. Four words, and the story lands right on David. I bet that room went dead quiet.
Quiet and hidden is how David acted, not how the LORD answers. He says, “…I will do this thing in broad daylight before all Israel.” Daylight, before all Israel. Nothing quiet about it.

Dark of night is where secrets like to live. But the LORD says, “…I will do this thing in broad daylight before all Israel.” The secret was David's, and the daylight is the LORD's answer. This is a heavy word.
David says it plain: “I have sinned against the LORD.” No excuses, no long speech. He owns it. Nathan answers right away, “The LORD has taken away your sin…”
Jonathan was David's close friend (1 Samuel 18:1), and he isn't the name here. The text says, “…they named him Solomon.” Good name, just not for this baby.
